name: Pind Hospitality
issue_size: ₹17.82 Cr (fresh only, 18,00,000 shares including 91,200 shares/₹0.9029 Cr reserved for Market Maker; net offer to public 17,08,800 shares aggregating ~₹17 Cr)
lm_rationale: Fedex Securities — chittorgarh 2026 SME tracker: 1 issue (ABH Healthcare, listed 1 Sep 2026), 0% positive, 100% negative, -7.79% avg listing gain — its only 2026 listing so far is negative. However its multi-year record on ipomarkets.com is stronger: 53 IPOs handled since 2019 (50 SME + 3 mainboard, including Mukka Proteins +42.9% and Patel Retail +17.6% on the mainboard side), +15.4% average listing gain across 50 listed issues. Weak current-year sample (n=1, negative) against a decent all-time average — classified Mixed rather than Solid/Strong given the most recent data point is negative.
valuation_text: attractive vs disclosed peers — 26.12x post-issue P/E sits below even the RHP's lowest peer P/E of 31.70x (peer average 191.57x, but PAT declined 11% YoY and leverage/liquidity are weakening
pbv: 4.29 (chittorgarh KPI table figure; could not be reconciled against NAV ₹34.59 at either the floor or cap price — see discrepancies)
net_proceeds: ₹12.70 Cr (₹1,269.81 lakhs) for capital expenditure on a hotel-cum-banquet hall ('Haveli Project') in Lonavala, Maharashtra (total project cost ₹2,142.38 lakhs, of which ₹872.47 lakhs already spent from internal accruals/borrowings); remainder of net proceeds for general corporate purposes, capped at the lower of 15% of gross proceeds or ₹1,000.00 lakhs (RHP leaves the exact GCP amount as [●] pending price finalisation).
key_risks: PAT fell 11.33% in FY26 (₹2.27 Cr vs ₹2.56 Cr in FY25) even as revenue grew 7.53%, on rising finance costs; Debt-Equity rose from 0.71 to 0.88 (+24.03%) as the company borrowed for the Haveli Project; Current Ratio fell to 0.90 (from 1.12), i.e. below 1, signalling tighter short-term liquidity; ROE/ROCE have declined for three straight years (ROE 22.85%→20.92%→15.65%, ROCE 16.18%→19.64%→15.83%); 78.38% of FY26 revenue came from third-party food delivery apps (₹1,916.48 lakhs), exposing the company to aggregator commission and negotiating-power risk; top-10 suppliers were 93.52% of FY26 purchases.
market_moat: Operates six restaurants in Pune (no permanent closures since 2016) plus outdoor catering and a majority (97.50%) partnership stake in Pind Punjab; over 5 lakh cumulative deliveries and recognised as a long-standing Pune restaurant partner on third-party food delivery apps; expanding into hospitality via the Haveli Project, a Punjabi-village-themed hotel-cum-banquet hall targeting the Lonavala destination-wedding and corporate-conference market.
management: Promoters Nimish Parveen Malhotra, Chirag Parveen Malhotra and Anita Malhotra hold 35,57,162 shares, 84.72% pre-issue, falling to 59.30% post-issue.
prose_business: Pune-based restaurant and hospitality operator, incorporated June 2021, running six restaurants under the Pind Punjab brand plus outdoor catering, and expanding into hotel/banquet operations via the Haveli Project in Lonavala. Revenue from operations grew from ₹2,077.79 lakhs in FY24 to ₹2,445.09 lakhs in FY26 (RHP KPI: +7.97% FY26 growth), but restated PAT fell from ₹256.23 lakhs in FY25 to ₹227.30 lakhs in FY26 as finance costs rose.
highlight_dev: The RHP discloses that outdoor catering revenue grew sharply from ₹64.38 lakhs (FY24) to ₹125.37 lakhs (FY25) to ₹528.61 lakhs (FY26), a new and fast-growing revenue line versus the core dine-in/delivery restaurant business.
sector_outlook: No third-party industry report is cited in the RHP's Objects of the Issue or Basis for Issue Price sections for hospitality/QSR sector sizing (unlike Nityas' CareEdge citation) — sector context here rests on company-specific disclosures only.
gov_scheme: Not applicable — no Government scheme or tender dependency disclosed.
peer_sentence: The RHP's Basis for Issue Price discloses only an Industry Peer Group P/E range — Highest 351.44x, Lowest 31.70x (negative P/E peers excluded), Average 191.57x — without naming individual peer companies; Pind's own post-issue P/E of 26.12x is below even the RHP's stated lowest peer P/E of 31.70x, implying a steep valuation discount versus the (thin, high-multiple) disclosed peer range.
verdict_reason: Priced well below its own disclosed peer range (26.12x vs 191.57x average, 31.70x lowest), but FY26 PAT fell 11.33%, D/E rose to 0.88 and current ratio dropped below 1 — the discount may reflect real deterioration, not just an SME-market pricing gap
why: Revenue from operations grew 7.97% to ₹24.45 Cr in FY26 (chittorgarh's Total Income figure of ₹24.91 Cr includes other income), but restated PAT fell 11.33% to ₹2.27 Cr as finance costs increased; RoNW/ROCE of 15.65%/15.83% are down from 20.92%/19.64% a year earlier. At ₹99 the issue prices at 26.12x post-issue EPS and a chittorgarh-stated P/BV of 4.29 (unreconciled against the disclosed NAV of ₹34.59 — see discrepancies) — the P/E figure is notably below the RHP's own disclosed peer range (191.57x average, 31.70x lowest, 351.44x highest), a wide discount for a thinly-comparable hospitality/restaurant peer set. ₹12.70 Cr of the ₹17.82 Cr issue funds a new Haveli Project hotel-cum-banquet hall in Lonavala, a genuine growth capex use, but the company is simultaneously carrying more debt (D/E up from 0.71 to 0.88) and its current ratio has slipped below 1 (0.90). Lead manager Fedex Securities' only 2026 SME listing (ABH Healthcare) is negative (-7.79%), though its multi-year record (53 IPOs, +15.4% avg listing gain) is more solid.
suggestion: Watch rather than apply blind — the low headline P/E is attractive on paper, but a declining-profit, rising-leverage SME issue with a negative-this-year lead manager and thin sub-₹1 current ratio deserves caution until subscription data and Haveli Project execution progress are visible

discrepancies: Chittorgarh's Company Financials table labels the ₹24.91/23.17/20.87 Cr row 'Total Income' (FY26/25/24); the RHP's own KPI table (Basis for Issue Price, p.98) discloses 'Revenue from Operations' of ₹2,445.09/2,264.56/2,077.79 lakhs (= ₹24.4509/22.6456/20.7779 Cr) for the same years — the small gap is other income; chittorgarh's revenue-growth narrative ('increased by 8%') matches the RHP KPI's disclosed FY26 growth of 7.97% closely enough that both are treated as consistent, with revenue-from-operations preferred as the RHP KPI figure.

Chittorgarh's KPI table shows 'Price to Book Value: 4.29' alongside NAV ₹34.59; recomputing 4.29 × 34.59 implies an effective price of ₹148.35, which does not match either the floor (₹93), cap (₹99), or any post-issue NAV variant computed from the RHP's disclosed pre-issue net worth/share counts. This figure could not be independently reconciled from RHP data and is reported as chittorgarh states it, flagged as unverified rather than corrected or discarded.

RHP's Basis for Issue Price P/E section (p.96) discloses only industry-peer-group P/E statistics (Highest 351.44x, Lowest 31.70x, Average 191.57x, based on BSE/NSE closing prices as of 18 Sep 2026) with NO named peer companies — unlike Nityas' RHP, which names its peers individually. Chittorgarh's page does not surface this peer range at all; it is added here from the RHP directly.

Chittorgarh's IPO Objects of the Issue table shows only 'Funding towards capital expenditure...(Haveli Project)' ₹12.70 Cr with a blank GCP amount, totalling ₹12.70 Cr; the RHP confirms ₹1,269.81 lakhs (=₹12.6981 Cr, chittorgarh rounds to ₹12.70 Cr) for the Haveli Project with GCP capped at the LOWER of 15% of gross proceeds or ₹1,000.00 lakhs — a two-part cap not visible on chittorgarh's page, added here.

Chittorgarh's promoter shareholding (84.72% pre / 59.30% post) matches the RHP's Capital Structure and Shareholding Pattern sections exactly (35,57,162 shares = 84.72% pre-issue, same shares = 59.30% post-issue) — no discrepancy, confirmed.

Chittorgarh's KPI table (ROE 15.65%, ROCE 15.83%, D/E 0.88, RoNW 15.65%, PAT margin 9.30%, EBITDA margin 16.14%, NAV ₹34.59) matches the RHP's Basis for Issue Price KPI table (p.98) and the Ratio Analysis annexure (p.196) exactly for FY26 — no discrepancy, confirmed.
